name: AutoSubSync
description: Automatically synchronizes external and embedded subtitles across your library, aligning each one against the audio of the media it belongs to. Where a wanted language has no subtitle at all, it can download one through the subtitle provider plugins you already have installed, and keeps it only when the audio check confirms it. The sync engine is downloaded once on first use and verified against a checksum built into the plugin.
overview: Automatically synchronizes external and embedded subtitles across your library, and can download one where a wanted language has none.

versions.changelog: Cuts what the download feature spends on subtitles it always discards. A candidate a provider names as hearing-impaired is now skipped before it costs a download, and a name saying the annotations have been removed is no longer mistaken for one. An item whose whole download budget went on hearing-impaired files it discarded is reported as a skip rather than as a failure of the audio check, which never saw them. Once an item has spent its download limit for a language it no longer buys a fresh budget on every scan; raising the limit is what lets it try again, and candidates already tried are still never bought twice. Hearing-impaired detection now logs how many cues were marked out of the total.

The plugin can now download a subtitle for a language an item has none of at all, using the subtitle provider plugins you already have installed and credentialled. It adds no provider and stores no account of its own. A downloaded subtitle is kept only when the audio check confirms it against the video's own audio; anything it will not confirm is discarded before it reaches your library, so an item can spend a download and still end up with nothing. Downloading is off by default and does nothing until you list the languages you want. New settings cover a per-item download limit, whether an embedded track counts as already covered, whether hearing-impaired subtitles are acceptable, and the order your providers are asked in. The settings page reports whether a download provider is installed and flags a provider name that matches nothing. Rollback deletes downloaded subtitles like anything else the plugin created, and keeps its record of candidates already tried and refused so they are not bought a second time.

A subtitle the plugin has already synced now stays in the synced count. Earlier versions could move it into the skipped group on a later run, so the synced total fell over time with nothing having actually changed. Stored results are re-judged once more as each subtitle is processed, so run a full library sync after updating to settle the counts. When the audio check finds a subtitle in sync but the title is too short for it to measure drift across, voice detection now reads that drift instead, which allows some syncs that were previously refused. A subtitle removed as a duplicate no longer returns when only stale metadata still offers it. The status panel names the version of the bundled sync engine rather than its packaging revision. The plugin is now licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0.

When the audio check cannot decide on a subtitle, a second pass now reads the same audio with voice detection and scores the subtitle against detected speech, which settles some of the titles the first pass could never measure. The check is also stricter about what counts as in sync: it judges alignment against the small lead subtitles are authored with rather than against zero, so results that are close but wrong are refused instead of written. Verdicts recorded by earlier versions were measured by the older rule and are re-judged as each subtitle is processed again, so run a full library sync after updating. A sync refused for rescaling the subtitle now says whether the title was simply too short for the check to measure drift. The sync engine has been rebuilt and downloads once more after this update.

A subtitle the plugin removed as a duplicate of an embedded track no longer returns to the synced count on the next scan, and deduplication no longer stops running for that language once it has removed one. When two copies are otherwise equal, deduplication now keeps the one that was in your library first. A track that a setting deliberately left alone is reported as set aside rather than listed as unsupported. The pipeline table drops its Rejected column, and a subtitle the audio check rejected is no longer counted as a synchronization failure there — the rejected by audio check card and its reason list already report it. Retry failed subtitles now says that it retries what the audio check rejected as well.

Duplicates the plugin removed are now counted in the pipeline table instead of disappearing from it, and removals from earlier runs are restored to it. Image tracks skipped because a text subtitle of the same language already covers them are listed as unsupported rather than going unreported. The audio check column no longer appears on pipeline steps the audio check does not run, and subtitles awaiting a dry run are no longer counted as already in sync. The median shift is reported as a distance and negative shifts display correctly, reason lists are no longer cut off after eight entries, and the panel shows when its counts were last updated.

The status panel counts rejected subtitles separately from failed ones, so the pipeline table no longer reports a rejection by the audio check as a synchronization failure. Failure reasons no longer show raw output from the sync engine or the OCR tool, and reason lines no longer repeat the heading they are listed under. A subtitle the engine rescaled past the framerate limit is reported as a failure rather than a rejection, and the audio check setting now says which rejections unticking it will release.

The status panel no longer counts subtitles that are gone from your library, and a subtitle removed as a duplicate stops counting in the same run rather than on the next scan. Retry failed subtitles now starts a full library sync as well. Adds a setting, Run the OCR when a text subtitle of the same language exists, and embedded tracks that an external subtitle already covers are now skipped by default; turn on Process embedded tracks when an external subtitle of the same language exists to keep converting them. Deduplication keeps the unnumbered filename when it picks which copy survives, a .sub with no .idx beside it now says why it cannot be read, and subtitles the engine moved less than the minimum are no longer counted as audio check failures.

A VobSub track holding several languages is now read as one subtitle per language instead of one file containing all of them. OCR output the reader could not resolve is refused rather than written to your library, and image subtitles are read with the right OCR model, including per-script Chinese and Serbian. The status panel now separates a refusal by the audio check from a tool failure, and adds cards for tracks whose source file has gone and tracks not yet run. More titles can be measured by the audio check instead of being left unjudged.

A sync the audio check cannot confirm is no longer written to your library. 1.2.5.0 could stretch a correctly timed subtitle when the audio check reached no verdict and the sync engine reported a small framerate correction; if any of your subtitles are wrong, Roll back everything restores your originals. A new setting, Only sync when audio check is conclusive, is on by default and refuses anything the audio cannot vouch for. The sync engine must now score an alignment of 40 a second, up from 20, and a stretch the audio check never measured is refused. Adds a Retry failed subtitles button under Actions, and stopping the scheduled task now stops syncs started by any other route.

The audio check no longer refuses subtitles it could not actually measure. A sync the engine finished is now kept even when the engine crashes reporting the result, and a subtitle the audio check cannot measure is refused only if the sync engine found no alignment either. Audio check refusals are grouped into readable rows in the log.

Every subtitle is now scored against the video's own audio, before and after syncing. A subtitle the audio already agrees with is left alone and never handed to the engine, and a result the audio disagrees with is discarded instead of written to your library. Results produced before 1.2.4.0 were never checked against the audio; if any of them are wrong, Roll back everything restores your originals. Maximum offset and Minimum offset are gone, automatic sync on new media and refresh after sync now default to off, and the status panel separates subtitles refused by the audio check from failures.
